title: The Amateur Emigrant · ship-travel excerpt
instructions: 真人历史作品朗读，非现代场景对话或官方试卷。先独立听音并完成6题，再提交核对；录制署名不出题。级别只是编写目标，未做真实考生难度标定。来源与署名可在开始后查看；若打开外部全文或原音，后续继续按已见材料记录。
transcript:
I first encountered my fellow-passengers on the Broomielaw in Glasgow. Thence we descended the Clyde in no familiar spirit, but looking askance on each other as on possible enemies. A few Scandinavians, who had already grown acquainted on the North Sea, were friendly and voluble over their long pipes; but among English speakers distance and suspicion reigned supreme. The sun was soon overclouded, the wind freshened and grew sharp as we continued to descend the widening estuary; and with the falling temperature the gloom among the passengers increased. Two of the women wept. Any one who had come aboard might have supposed we were all absconding from the law. There was scarce a word interchanged, and no common sentiment but that of cold united us, until at length, having touched at Greenock, a pointing arm and rush to the starboard bow announced that our ocean steamer was in sight. There she lay in mid-river, at the tail of the Bank, her sea-signal flying: a wall of bulwark, a street of white deck-houses, an aspiring forest of spars, larger than a church, and soon to be as populous as many an incorporated town in the land to which she was to bear us.
I was not, in truth, a steerage passenger. Although anxious to see the worst of emigrant life, I had some work to finish on the voyage, and was advised to go by the second cabin, where at least I should have a table at command. The advice was excellent; but to understand the choice, and what I gained, some outline of the internal disposition of the ship will first be necessary.
transcriptScope: 完整所选正文；完整音轨中的 LibriVox 开头/结尾署名不在正文转录内。标点和大小写按印刷文本规范；不把机器识别结果当作精确逐字听写。

questions.prompt: In which city did the narrator first meet the other passengers? Write ONE WORD.
questions.evidence: I first encountered my fellow-passengers on the Broomielaw in Glasgow.
questions.explanation: Broomielaw 是当地地点；城市名是 Glasgow。

questions.prompt: Why were some Scandinavian passengers already friendly with one another?
options: They all worked for the ship’s owner.
They had grown up in the same town.
They had become acquainted on an earlier sea crossing.
answers: They had become acquainted on an earlier sea crossing.
questions.evidence: A few Scandinavians, who had already grown acquainted on the North Sea
questions.explanation: North Sea 上已结识是明确原因，不可推断同乡或同事。

questions.prompt: What happened to the passengers’ mood as the temperature fell?
options: It changed from fear to excitement.
questions.evidence: with the falling temperature the gloom among the passengers increased.
questions.explanation: gloom ... increased 说明低落加重；不是变得愉快。

questions.prompt: How many women cried? Write ONE WORD.
questions.explanation: wept 是 cried 的过去式同义表达。

questions.prompt: What caused people to point and rush to the bow?
options: Their ocean steamer came into view.
answers: Their ocean steamer came into view.
questions.evidence: a pointing arm and rush to the starboard bow announced that our ocean steamer was in sight.
questions.explanation: in sight 解释人们朝船头聚集；未提到落水或风暴损坏。

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator choose the second cabin?
options: He had been refused all other accommodation.
He needed a table for work during the voyage.
He wanted to travel with a large family.
answers: He needed a table for work during the voyage.
questions.evidence: I had some work to finish on the voyage, and was advised to go by the second cabin, where at least I should have a table at command.
questions.explanation: 工作及桌子是实际选择原因；想体验移民生活不等于选择统舱。
